description: List events from the user's connected calendars, Google and Outlook together, ordered by start time: summary, start/end, location, organizer, attendees and their RSVP status, a meeting link when there is one, and which provider and account each event came from (Outlook events carry a web_link that opens them in Outlook). With no time range it returns upcoming events from now. For one whole day ('who am I meeting today', 'what's on tomorrow', 'Friday the 21st') pass `day`: 'today', 'tomorrow', 'yesterday' or a date YYYY-MM-DD, read midnight to midnight in the user's timezone, the same day the Today page shows. Otherwise `time_min` and `time_max` are RFC3339 timestamps built from the current date in the system prompt; past ranges work too. Every result carries `owner_clock` (the user's timezone, now and today): if the range you read is not the day the user asked about, read again before answering. `query` free-text matches event titles, descriptions, and attendees, so an empty result with a query means nothing matched it, not that the calendar is clear. If the result has `accounts_failed` or an `error`, those calendars were not read: say so and never call the calendar clear on the strength of a partial or failed read. For 'how many meetings' questions over long ranges (a quarter, a year), set count_only=true; it sweeps the whole range and returns the total plus a per-month breakdown instead of the events themselves, so a 12-month count is one call. By default this reads each account's main calendar. When a Google account can list its calendars, the result carries available_calendars (name, id, access role), shared calendars included: pass a calendar's name or id as calendar_id ('Family') to read it, or all_calendars=true to read every calendar at once. For an Outlook calendar, get its id from list_outlook_calendars. If the result says no calendar is connected (or the account lacks calendar access), show the user the message and link them to https://youspot.com/user/integrations/gmail.

account.description: Email address of one connected Google account or Outlook mailbox. Omit to read all connected calendars.

all_calendars.description: Read every Google calendar the user can see events on, shared ones included, instead of just the main one. Each event then names its calendar.

calendar_id.description: Which calendar to read: a name or id from available_calendars, or an id from list_google_calendars or list_outlook_calendars. Omit for each account's main calendar.

count_only.description: Return only counts (total and per calendar month) instead of the events. Sweeps far more of the range (up to 12,500 events) than an event listing can. Use for totals and "how many" questions.

day.description: One whole day in the user's timezone: 'today', 'tomorrow', 'yesterday' or 'YYYY-MM-DD'. Replaces time_min and time_max.

query.description: Free-text search over events (titles, descriptions, attendees). Omit to list everything in the range.

time_min.description: Earliest event end, RFC3339 ('2026-08-19T00:00:00Z'). Defaults to now when time_max is also omitted.

name: get_calendar_events
title: Get calendar events
